mcq.q: Winter pruning is carried out mainly to
choices: B Set the number of buds, and therefore yield, for the coming season
mcq.answer: B Set the number of buds, and therefore yield, for the coming season
mcq.why: Spur or cane pruning decides next year’s crop before the vine wakes.

mcq.q: Diurnal range (warm days, cold nights) tends to
choices: B Help grapes keep acidity while still ripening flavour and sugar by day
C Prevent any colour in red grapes
mcq.answer: B Help grapes keep acidity while still ripening flavour and sugar by day
mcq.why: Altitude and continental nights are classic tools for freshness in warm regions.

mcq.q: Botrytis cinerea is ‘noble’ only when
choices: A It always rots the bunches in wet weather with no sun
B Humid nights and dry days desiccate ripe berries without grey rot
C It attacks green, unripe fruit in spring
D It is sprayed on as sulphur
mcq.answer: B Humid nights and dry days desiccate ripe berries without grey rot
mcq.why: The same fungus is grey rot in wet, tight, unripe bunches.

mcq.q: A north-facing slope in the northern hemisphere generally
choices: A Is the warmest option at every latitude
B Receives less direct sun and is cooler than a south-facing slope
C Always ripens Cabernet better than a south face
D Has no effect on frost
mcq.answer: B Receives less direct sun and is cooler than a south-facing slope
mcq.why: Aspect is a primary site factor; in the southern hemisphere the warm face is north.

mcq.q: Thermovinification of red grapes is used mainly to
choices: A Keep a long, cool carbonic ferment
B Extract colour quickly with heat, then ferment a must with little tannin
mcq.answer: B Extract colour quickly with heat, then ferment a must with little tannin
mcq.why: A bulk-wine tool for colour without a long maceration.

mcq.q: Fining a red wine with egg white is traditionally used to
choices: B Soften tannin and help clarity
mcq.answer: B Soften tannin and help clarity
mcq.why: Albumin binds harsher tannins; bentonite is more for protein in whites.

mcq.q: Sterile filtration before bottling a wine with residual sugar is done to
choices: A Add yeast for a second ferment in bottle
B Remove microbes that could referment
mcq.answer: B Remove microbes that could referment
mcq.why: Sweet and off-dry wines need microbiological stability.

mcq.q: A portion of stems in a Pinot Noir ferment is used to
choices: B Add structure, perfume and a slightly higher pH if stems are ripe
mcq.answer: B Add structure, perfume and a slightly higher pH if stems are ripe
mcq.why: Whole bunch is a style tool; green stems add harshness, not perfume.

mcq.q: Haut-Médoc as an appellation covers
choices: B The communes south of the Médoc AOC that are not a village AOC, plus a regional frame for the famous villages
mcq.answer: B The communes south of the Médoc AOC that are not a village AOC, plus a regional frame for the famous villages
mcq.why: Many crus bourgeois are Haut-Médoc; Pauillac etc. are more specific village AOCs.

mcq.q: Lalande-de-Pomerol is
choices: B A satellite red AOC next to Pomerol, Merlot-led
mcq.answer: B A satellite red AOC next to Pomerol, Merlot-led
mcq.why: Usually a step down in price from Pomerol proper.

mcq.q: Chambolle-Musigny is reputed for
choices: A The sturdiest, most tannic Nuits style
B Particularly perfumed Côte de Nuits Pinot Noir
C Only white Grand Cru Chardonnay
mcq.answer: B Particularly perfumed Côte de Nuits Pinot Noir
mcq.why: Musigny and Bonnes-Mares sit here; the village stereotype is silk and perfume.

mcq.q: Mâcon-Lugny or Mâcon-Azé on a label means
choices: D A Priorat vi de vila
mcq.answer: B A village-named Mâconnais Chardonnay
mcq.why: Better than generic Mâcon-Villages when the village is named.

mcq.q: Savennières Roche-aux-Moines is
choices: B A named dry Chenin site within Savennières
mcq.answer: B A named dry Chenin site within Savennières
mcq.why: Coulée de Serrant is the other famous named Savennières site.

mcq.q: Cheverny’s everyday white is often
choices: B Sauvignon Blanc, sometimes with Chardonnay; Cour-Cheverny is the Romorantin AOC beside it
mcq.answer: B Sauvignon Blanc, sometimes with Chardonnay; Cour-Cheverny is the Romorantin AOC beside it
mcq.why: Two neighbouring AOCs; do not mix the grapes up.

mcq.q: Clairette de Die is
choices: A A dry Northern Rhône Syrah
B A sweetish, low-alcohol sparkling wine from the Diois, often Muscat-based (méthode ancestrale for the Tradition)
mcq.answer: B A sweetish, low-alcohol sparkling wine from the Diois, often Muscat-based (méthode ancestrale for the Tradition)
mcq.why: East of the Northern Rhône proper; Crémant de Die is the drier traditional-method wine.

mcq.q: Beaumes-de-Venise as a still red (not the Muscat) is
choices: B A Southern Rhône village red, Grenache-based
mcq.answer: B A Southern Rhône village red, Grenache-based
mcq.why: The village has both a VDN Muscat and a Côtes du Rhône-Villages-style red AOC.

mcq.q: Madiran is the South-West AOC for
choices: B Tannat, a highly tannic red that often sees micro-oxygenation or long élevage
mcq.answer: B Tannat, a highly tannic red that often sees micro-oxygenation or long élevage
mcq.why: Tannat needs ripe fruit and time; Irouléguy is a smaller Tannat neighbour.

mcq.q: Sélection de Grains Nobles (SGN) in Alsace is
choices: B A botrytis selection at a very high must weight, always sweet
mcq.answer: B A botrytis selection at a very high must weight, always sweet
mcq.why: Rarer and sweeter than Vendange Tardive; noble varieties.

mcq.q: Carema and Donnas are
choices: B Alpine Nebbiolo (Piedmont/Aosta), lighter and more scented than Barolo
mcq.answer: B Alpine Nebbiolo (Piedmont/Aosta), lighter and more scented than Barolo
mcq.why: High terraces; a different Nebbiolo conversation from the Langhe.

mcq.q: Rosso di Montalcino is
choices: B The earlier-released Sangiovese from the Brunello zone
mcq.answer: B The earlier-released Sangiovese from the Brunello zone
mcq.why: Same grape and zone, shorter ageing — a younger sibling, not a different variety.

mcq.q: Prosecco DOC still (tranquillo) exists, but the region’s fame is
choices: B Sparkling Glera; the still wine is a minor part of the offer
mcq.answer: B Sparkling Glera; the still wine is a minor part of the offer
mcq.why: Do not assume every bottle from Conegliano is sparkling — but most are.

mcq.q: Aglianico del Vulture and Taurasi are
choices: B Southern Italian Aglianico reds, high acid and tannin, built to age
mcq.answer: B Southern Italian Aglianico reds, high acid and tannin, built to age
mcq.why: Vulture is Basilicata (volcanic); Taurasi is Campania DOCG.

mcq.q: Somontano in Aragón has a reputation for
choices: A Only bush-vine Garnacha with no internationals
B A mix of local and international varieties in a relatively cool Pyrenean-foot climate
mcq.answer: B A mix of local and international varieties in a relatively cool Pyrenean-foot climate
mcq.why: Chardonnay, Gewurz and Cabernet sit beside Moristel and Garnacha.

mcq.q: Rueda Verdejo that has seen oak or lees will typically be
choices: B Fuller and more textured than a straight stainless version
mcq.answer: B Fuller and more textured than a straight stainless version
mcq.why: Most Rueda is tank-fresh; a minority is built for more weight.

mcq.q: Navarra, next to Rioja, is known for
choices: B Rosé (Garnacha) and a mix of Tempranillo and international reds
mcq.answer: B Rosé (Garnacha) and a mix of Tempranillo and international reds
mcq.why: Historically rosado; now a broader still-wine DO.

mcq.q: Baden is Germany’s
choices: B Warmest large region, a source of Spätburgunder and fuller whites
mcq.answer: B Warmest large region, a source of Spätburgunder and fuller whites
mcq.why: Kaiserstuhl volcanic warmth; Pinot family does well.

mcq.q: Santorini’s basket-trained (kouloura) vines exist mainly to
choices: B Protect buds and fruit from wind and to manage water on volcanic soils
mcq.answer: B Protect buds and fruit from wind and to manage water on volcanic soils
mcq.why: Windswept island; Assyrtiko trained low in wreaths.

mcq.q: Bucelas near Lisbon is a historic AOC for
mcq.answer: B Dry, high-acid Arinto whites
mcq.why: Atlantic-influenced white; Arinto keeps acid in the warmth.

mcq.q: Douro Superior is
choices: A The coolest, wettest Port sub-zone
B The hottest, driest inland sub-zone, opened more recently to planting
mcq.answer: B The hottest, driest inland sub-zone, opened more recently to planting
mcq.why: Baixo Corgo wettest; Cima Corgo classic heart; Superior the frontier heat.

mcq.q: Oakville and Rutherford AVAs sit in
choices: B The Napa Valley floor, associated with Cabernet Sauvignon
mcq.answer: B The Napa Valley floor, associated with Cabernet Sauvignon
mcq.why: Bench and floor sites; ‘Rutherford dust’ is local lore for a dusty tannin feel.

mcq.q: Leyda and San Antonio in Chile are
choices: B Cool coastal valleys for Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay and Pinot Noir
mcq.answer: B Cool coastal valleys for Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay and Pinot Noir
mcq.why: Closer to the Pacific than Casablanca in places; marked acidity.

mcq.q: McLaren Vale, south of Adelaide, is known for
choices: A Only bone-dry Riesling like Clare
B Shiraz and GSM in a warm, Gulf-moderated climate, often with old vines
mcq.answer: B Shiraz and GSM in a warm, Gulf-moderated climate, often with old vines
mcq.why: Mediterranean; a little more breeze than Barossa; Grenache revival.

mcq.q: Central Otago sub-zones such as Bannockburn and Gibbston differ mainly in
choices: A Grape variety by law (only Sauvignon in Gibbston)
B Altitude and heat: Gibbston cooler, Bannockburn riper Pinot
mcq.answer: B Altitude and heat: Gibbston cooler, Bannockburn riper Pinot
mcq.why: One region, several mesoclimates; all Pinot-led.

mcq.q: A Canadian VQA wine, if it names a provincial GI, must be
choices: A A blend from any country
B 100% from that province under the VQA rules
mcq.answer: B 100% from that province under the VQA rules
mcq.why: VQA is the quality/origin system in Ontario and British Columbia.

mcq.q: South African Wine of Origin (WO) on a label means
choices: B The grapes come from the stated estate, ward, district or region under WO law
C The wine is always Pinotage
mcq.answer: B The grapes come from the stated estate, ward, district or region under WO law
mcq.why: WO is the PDO-like hierarchy: estate < ward < district < region.

mcq.q: ‘Contains sulphites’ on a label is
choices: B A mandatory allergen-style declaration when SO2 is above a low threshold
C Proof the wine is faulty
mcq.answer: B A mandatory allergen-style declaration when SO2 is above a low threshold
mcq.why: Almost all wine must carry it; it is not a quality statement.

mcq.q: A Champagne labelled Blanc de Blancs is made from
choices: B White grapes only — in practice Chardonnay
C A red still wine blend
mcq.answer: B White grapes only — in practice Chardonnay
mcq.why: Almost always Côte des Blancs Chardonnay; leaner, more citrus, ages to toast.

mcq.q: The ancestral method (méthode ancestrale) relies on
choices: A A complete dry first ferment then a sugared tirage like Champagne
B Bottling a still-fermenting wine so the last sugar makes the bubbles
mcq.answer: B Bottling a still-fermenting wine so the last sugar makes the bubbles
mcq.why: One ferment, often cloudy, lower pressure; Clairette de Die Tradition, some Pét-nat.

mcq.q: Cava de Paraje Calificado is
choices: B A single-vineyard, long-aged top tier of Cava
mcq.answer: B A single-vineyard, long-aged top tier of Cava
mcq.why: Stricter ripeness, yield and lees rules than basic Cava.

mcq.q: Tasmania is important to Australian sparkling wine because
choices: A It is the hottest GI
B It is cool enough for high-acid Chardonnay and Pinot base wines
C It produces only fortified Muscat
mcq.answer: B It is cool enough for high-acid Chardonnay and Pinot base wines
mcq.why: Many mainland houses source base wine from the island.

mcq.q: Sec on a sparkling label is
choices: B Sweeter than Extra Dry (about 17–32 g/L)
mcq.answer: B Sweeter than Extra Dry (about 17–32 g/L)
mcq.why: The French word ‘sec’ is misleading on sparkling wine.

mcq.q: A Fino that is bottled and then stored warm for a year will typically
choices: B Lose freshness and taste tired or oxidised
mcq.answer: B Lose freshness and taste tired or oxidised
mcq.why: Biological Sherries are fragile after bottling; buy recently bottled stock.

mcq.q: Single Quinta Vintage Port is
choices: B A vintage-dated Port from one estate, often declared in years that are not a general declaration
mcq.answer: B A vintage-dated Port from one estate, often declared in years that are not a general declaration
mcq.why: A house can bottle a quinta in a good-but-not-great year.

mcq.q: Verdelho Madeira sits on the sweetness scale
choices: B Between dry Sercial and medium-sweet Bual
mcq.answer: B Between dry Sercial and medium-sweet Bual
mcq.why: Sercial – Verdelho – Bual – Malmsey is the classic ladder.

mcq.q: Rivesaltes and Banyuls differ from Port mainly in
choices: B Grapes, climate and often a more oxidative or Grenache/Muscat flavour, though mutage is the same idea
D Using only Palomino under flor
mcq.answer: B Grapes, climate and often a more oxidative or Grenache/Muscat flavour, though mutage is the same idea
mcq.why: Same fortify-while-sweet idea; different place and varieties.

mcq.q: Commandaria is
choices: B A historic sweet wine from Cyprus, from sun-dried grapes, sometimes fortified
mcq.answer: B A historic sweet wine from Cyprus, from sun-dried grapes, sometimes fortified
mcq.why: Mavro and Xynisteri; WSET mentions it among sweet/fortified oddities.

mcq.q: A wine that is ‘hazy’ on appearance may be
choices: A Automatically faulty in every case
B Unfiltered and acceptable, or unstable and faulty — judge with the nose and palate
mcq.answer: B Unfiltered and acceptable, or unstable and faulty — judge with the nose and palate
mcq.why: Clarity is clear or hazy; haze plus off-aroma is the problem.

mcq.q: Full-bodied red wines such as Barolo or Napa Cabernet are usually served
choices: B At about 15–18 °C, not ‘room temperature’ of a warm modern room
mcq.answer: B At about 15–18 °C, not ‘room temperature’ of a warm modern room
mcq.why: Too warm emphasises alcohol; too cold emphasises tannin.

mcq.q: A dish with a sweet glaze needs a wine that is
choices: A Bone dry and high in tannin
B At least as sweet as the glaze
mcq.answer: B At least as sweet as the glaze
mcq.why: The same rule as dessert: the wine must not be drier than the food.

mcq.q: Intensity on the SAT nose is judged on the scale
choices: B Light / medium(−) / medium / medium(+) / pronounced
mcq.answer: B Light / medium(−) / medium / medium(+) / pronounced
mcq.why: Do not use pale/deep for aroma; do not write a range.

parts.prompt: Compare the key climate influences of Mendoza with those of Chile’s Central Valley and cool coastal valleys.
points: Mendoza: rain shadow of the Andes, high altitude, bright light, irrigation from meltwater, continental, hail risk.
Chile Central Valley (Maipo, Colchagua, Cachapoal): Andes + coastal range, warm, dry, irrigation, Humboldt is weaker inland.
Casablanca / San Antonio / Leyda: coastal, Humboldt fog and breeze, cooler, Sauvignon/Chardonnay/Pinot.
Both countries are dry in the growing season by the standards of Europe — disease pressure is lower.
El Niño / frost / hail as hazards.
Do not say Chile is ‘always cool’ or Mendoza is ‘tropical’.

parts.prompt: Why does altitude matter so much to Malbec and to Torrontés?
points: Altitude increases diurnal range: acid and colour (Malbec) and floral freshness (Torrontés) survive a sunny day.
Uco Valley vs lower Luján de Cuyo / Maipú: cooler, later, more floral Malbec.
Cafayate: very high, Torrontés stays aromatic and usually dry.
Too low and warm: jammy Malbec, blowsy Torrontés.
UV at height thickens skins.
Irrigation still needed — altitude is not rainfall.

parts.prompt: Outline typical winery choices for an inexpensive Chilean Cabernet versus a premium Uco Malbec.
points: Inexpensive Cabernet: machine harvest, crush, short-ish maceration, cultured yeast, oak chips or staves, early release, fruity.
Premium Malbec: sort, longer skin time, French oak (some new), 12–18 months, may include whole berry, bottled for ageing.
Both usually MLF.
Acidification is common in warm musts where law and house style allow.
State the style contrast.

written.title: Question 2 — Spain beyond Rioja: Priorat, Rías Baixas, Rueda

parts.prompt: For each of Priorat, Rías Baixas and Rueda, state climate, principal grape and a typical style.
points: Priorat: warm, dry, llicorella slopes; Garnacha and Cariñena; high alcohol, concentrated, often oak, DOCa.
Rías Baixas: cool, wet, Atlantic; Albariño; dry, high acid, peach/citrus, lees, drink young (some age).
Rueda: continental, quite high, frosty; Verdejo (± Sauvignon); dry, herbal, tank, everyday white.
One accurate extra detail per region (soil, blending partner, ageing) can score.
Do not relocate the grapes.

parts.prompt: What vineyard problem is typical in Rías Baixas, and how is it managed?
points: Rain and humidity: downy mildew, grey rot, diluted fruit.
Pérgola / tendone (parra) to lift fruit into the air and allow breeze.
Shoot thinning, spray programmes, canopy air.
Granite soils drain; site near the sea is cooler.
Hand harvest and sorting in quality wines.
Contrast with Priorat drought / low yield.

parts.prompt: Contrast winery choices for a concentrated Priorat tinto and a fresh Rueda Verdejo.
points: Priorat: low-yield fruit, destem, ferment on skins, often French oak, 12–20 months, MLF, built to age.
Rueda: protective, cool stainless, maybe lees, little new oak, bottled for early fruit.
Neither is fortified.
Priorat alcohol can be high; Rueda is moderate.
State the drink-window contrast.

written.title: Question 3 — Tank, transfer and traditional method

parts.prompt: Compare the three methods of making a fully sparkling wine: traditional, transfer and tank.
points: Traditional: second ferment in this bottle; riddling; disgorge; most autolysis; most labour.
Transfer: second ferment in bottle, then emptied to tank under pressure, filtered, rebottled — keeps bottle-ferment character, skips riddling.
Tank / Charmat / Martinotti: second ferment in tank, filtered to bottle; primary fruit; cheap; Prosecco, Asti, much Sekt.
All can set sweetness at the end (dosage or adjustment).
Ancestral as a fourth, if mentioned, is a single ferment.
Name a wine for each of the three main methods.

parts.prompt: When would a producer choose tank over traditional method?
points: Grape whose point is primary aroma (Glera, Muscat, Sauvignon).
Price point and volume.
Need to bottle and sell within months.
No wish for biscuit autolysis.
Easier to keep a consistent house sweetness.
Equipment already in the winery.

parts.prompt: What must you still get right in the vineyard for a tank-method wine to be more than just cheap fizz?
points: Ripe but not flabby fruit; enough acid.
Healthy grapes (rot shows in an aromatic, early wine).
Yield not so high that flavour disappears.
Site/climate suited to the variety (Prosecco hills vs plains).
Clean, cool handling after harvest.
Variety choice that matches the method.

written.title: Question 4 — Sherry solera and PX at the table

parts.prompt: Explain how a criadera-and-solera system works for a Fino, and why young wine is added.
points: Rows of butts: solera (oldest, from which you bottle) and several criaderas above.
Only a fraction is drawn each year; it is refreshed from the criadera above.
New vintage wine enters the youngest criadera.
Flor needs nutrients and a consistent strength/temperature — the refresh feeds it.
Style is consistent; no single vintage (unless a dated exception).
Biological vs the same hardware used oxidatively for Oloroso (no flor).

parts.prompt: How is PX made sweet, and how is it used both as a wine and as a sweetening tool?
points: Pedro Ximénez grapes sun-dried (asoleo), very high sugar, ferment barely starts, fortify, oxidative ageing.
Bottled as a luscious wine (raisin, molasses).
Blended into Oloroso to make Cream; into Fino-style to make Pale Cream.
Montilla is a major PX source.
Colour and sugar are extreme compared with Fino.
A little PX can also finish a sauce — but that is service, not winemaking.

parts.prompt: Pair a cold Fino and a room-cool PX with food, and state storage after opening.
points: Fino: chilled, olives, fried fish, jamón; fridge, a few days.
PX: slightly cool, vanilla ice cream, chocolate, blue cheese; lasts weeks, cool and recorked.
Do not cellar opened Fino; do not serve PX ice-cold or Fino at 20 °C.
Sweetness match for PX; salt/fat for Fino.
Fresh bottling date matters far more for Fino.
